- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to match momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the next 2–3 periods.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.5, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per period until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast from period 20 onward if sentiment remains positive.
